## Core question

The model may be identifiable in principle. But with the finite, noisy data we actually have,
can the parameter be estimated precisely enough to be useful? Practical non-identifiability is
a property of the **model together with the data**. More or better data can fix it.

## Definitions across fields

### Systems biology and dynamical systems

> A structurally identifiable parameter is practically non-identifiable if its likelihood-based
> confidence interval extends to infinity in at least one direction, given the available data.
> [@raue2009structural; @wieland2021structural]

### Econometrics (weak identification)

> A parameter is weakly identified when the data contain little information about it. In
> instrumental-variable and GMM settings, this happens when the instruments are only weakly
> related to the endogenous variables, and standard asymptotic approximations break down.
> [@stock2002survey]

### Bayesian inference

There is no single definition. A common working notion: the posterior for the parameter is
dominated by the prior, so the prior and posterior overlap heavily. In latent class models,
@garrett2000latent use the prior–posterior overlap of each parameter as a diagnostic.

## Formal statement

*(no single formal definition)* Each field operationalises the idea differently:

- profile-likelihood interval unbounded at a chosen confidence level [@raue2009structural];
- weak-instrument asymptotics, where identification strength shrinks with sample size
  [@stock2002survey];
- prior–posterior overlap above a threshold [@garrett2000latent].

## Examples

- An ODE model where a rate constant can be estimated only if the system is sampled during a
  fast transient that the design misses.
- Hierarchical models with few groups: the between-group variance is identifiable but very
  poorly estimated.
- Instrumental-variable analysis with a weak first stage. [@stock2002survey]

## Connections and distinctions

- **vs. [structural non-identifiability](structural-non-identifiability.qmd):** see that page.
  The profile likelihood is flat in the structural case, and finite but wide or one-sided in
  the practical case.
- **[Recoverability](recoverability.qmd):** *(proposed)* practical identifiability is
  identifiability judged at the precision the data can deliver; recoverability asks the same
  question about functionals.

## Key references

- @raue2009structural: the profile-likelihood definition.
- @wieland2021structural: review of the structural vs. practical distinction.
- @stock2002survey: weak identification in econometrics.

## Open questions

- *(open)* Is there a definition of practical identifiability that is not tied to a particular
  inferential framework (likelihood, GMM, Bayesian)?
- *(open)* How should practical identifiability be assessed for spatial and hierarchical models,
  where information differs by component and location?
